paper_metadata.title: Benchmarking Amplitude Estimation on a Superconducting Quantum Computer

summary: This paper benchmarks maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation on IBM Nairobi superconducting hardware using 2-qubit and 4-qubit inner-product estimation circuits. The authors report that optimized circuits reached a mean relative error of 0.0017 for the 2-qubit case and 0.0442 for the 4-qubit case, with the best 4-qubit result occurring after 3 Grover iterations and a circuit depth of 131.

experiments.description: Benchmarking maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation (MLE/MLAE) for estimating the inner product amplitude of two random 2-dimensional unit vectors on IBM Nairobi superconducting hardware, comparing ordinary transpilation, optimized transpilation, and naive sampling baselines.

algorithm.variant: Maximum Likelihood Amplitude Estimation (MLE/MLAE) with linear incremental sequence (LIS) schedule
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Fixed schedule up to 7 Grover iterations; 500 shots per iteration; repeated 50 times
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Uniform prior over theta in [0, pi/2]

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Unary data-loader / inner-product circuit encodes the squared inner product of two 2D unit vectors into the amplitude of the first qubit; Grover iterate Q = A S0 A† Sψ
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate amplitude a where sin^2(theta)=a and a corresponds to the squared inner product of two 2D unit vectors

problem_instance.description: Squared inner product estimation for two 2-dimensional unit vectors

dataset_specification.description: Two randomly generated 2D unit vectors; paper gives one example pair in the text

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Random unit vectors generated; inner product uniformly distributed
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each configuration run with 500 shots per Grover-iteration circuit, repeated 50 times; compared MLE output and naive sampling against exact inner product; mean relative error reported

transpilation_settings.optimization_level: standard transpilation and aggressive optimization levels (Qiskit level 3; Pytket level 2)

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Random unit vectors generated; circuits constructed in Qiskit and optimized with Qiskit and Pytket
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Maximum-likelihood estimation over measured counts; relative error computed against exact inner product

speedup_claims.conditions: Amplitude estimation convergence compared with classical sampling
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper states the asymptotic scaling O(1/M) versus O(1/sqrt(M)); this is a general AE claim, not a hardware-specific measured speedup.

speedup_claims.factor: outperformed naive sampling up to 3 Grover iterations
speedup_claims.conditions: On IBM Nairobi superconducting hardware with optimized circuits
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports that MLE using optimally compiled circuits outperformed naive sampling for up to 3 Grover iterations; exact naive-sampling error values are not provided.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 2-qubit superconducting QPU (IBM Nairobi), up to 7 Grover iterations, 500 shots per iteration, 50 repetitions
limiting_factors: deep compiled circuits for Grover iterations
classical baseline is naive sampling rather than a strong domain-specific classical solver

notes: Circuit depth for the 2D experiment is not explicitly stated; only the paper's general discussion of depths and the 4D benchmark provide explicit depth values.
The paper reports that MLE outperformed naive sampling for the 2-qubit case, but this is a benchmark result on a toy instance rather than evidence of practical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Benchmarking maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation (MLE/MLAE) for estimating the inner product amplitude of two random 4-dimensional unit vectors on IBM Nairobi superconducting hardware, comparing ordinary transpilation, optimized transpilation, and naive sampling baselines.

algorithm.variant: Maximum Likelihood Amplitude Estimation (MLE/MLAE) with linear incremental sequence (LIS) schedule
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Fixed schedule up to 7 Grover iterations; 500 shots per iteration; repeated 50 times
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Uniform prior over theta in [0, pi/2]

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Unary data-loader / inner-product circuit loads a 4-dimensional vector into amplitudes a|0001>+b|0010>+c|0100>+d|1000>; the amplitude of |0001> encodes the squared inner product of two 4D unit vectors
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate amplitude a where sin^2(theta)=a and a corresponds to the squared inner product of two 4D unit vectors

problem_instance.description: Squared inner product estimation for two random 4-dimensional unit vectors

dataset_specification.description: 50 random vector pairs; one example pair is given in the text; inner product uniformly distributed

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Random unit vectors generated; inner product uniformly distributed
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Experiment repeated 50 times; 500 shots per Grover-iteration circuit; compared MLE output and naive sampling against exact inner product; mean relative error reported

transpilation_settings.optimization_level: Qiskit level 3 and Pytket level 2 (most aggressive settings used)

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Random unit vectors generated; circuits constructed in Qiskit and optimized with Qiskit and Pytket
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Maximum-likelihood estimation over measured counts; relative error computed against exact inner product

speedup_claims.conditions: Amplitude estimation convergence compared with classical sampling
speedup_claims.caveats: General AE scaling claim; not a direct measured wall-clock speedup.

speedup_claims.factor: outperformed naive sampling and achieved mean error 0.0442
speedup_claims.conditions: IBM Nairobi superconducting hardware; optimized circuits; best result after 3 Grover iterations
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper states optimized circuits reduced error and that the best 4-qubit result was achieved after 3 Grover iterations with mean error 0.0442. Exact naive-sampling error values are not reported.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 4-qubit superconducting QPU (IBM Nairobi), up to 7 Grover iterations, 500 shots per iteration, 50 repetitions
limiting_factors: circuit depth around 131 even after optimization
comparison only against naive sampling, not a strong classical estimator

notes: The paper explicitly states the best 4-qubit result was achieved after 3 Grover iterations with mean error 0.0442 and that optimized circuits reached a maximum depth of around 131 for 3 Grover iterations.
The paper reports a best mean relative error of 0.0442 after 3 Grover iterations on optimized 4-qubit circuits, but does not establish practical advantage over strong classical methods.
